scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward Maltrata approach and entry into the Blanco corridor
correspondence.finding: The Maltrata relief map shows the selected western valley approach continuing east through the Maltrata urban-valley setting; the named Encino approach comes from the north. The state sheet continues this eastward approach through Nogales/Ciudad Mendoza into the river corridor south of Orizaba. The municipality's hydrography table independently lists Encino and Maltrata as intermittent currents within the Blanco sub-basin; the table alone is not used as geographic correspondence.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Central Río Blanco trunk
correspondence.finding: The original state sheet traces the selected Orizaba–Rafael Delgado/Ixtaczoquitlán corridor, its eastward and southeastward turns past the Tuxpanguillo–Cuichapa area, and continuation near Omealca and La Campana. Río Blanco is labeled on this continuous central corridor. The separately mapped Atoyac/Paso Blanco and more southerly Otapa approaches are not substituted for it.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower branching plain and southward wetland passage
correspondence.finding: The Tlalixcoyan relief map resolves the eastward Blanco trunk and the lower branching setting near Espinal/Tío Chico. The selected southward route corresponds to the connected Las Pozas wetland corridor, rather than the northeastern Blanco branch. The overlapping Ignacio de la Llave map carries the southern Las Pozas/Caño Largo and connected-waterbody setting eastward into the El Lodo/Limón lagoon-margin corridor shown regionally on the state sheet. This reads the material southern bend and eastward connector without assigning one name to the entire wetland network.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward lagoon-margin continuation and actual terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The Ignacio de la Llave and Alvarado maps overlap across the lower connected waters and northward lagoon-margin passage. The latter labels Laguna de Tlalixcoyan separately from Alvarado, Camaronera and the Papaloapan approach. The 1992 original field-study figure shows the Blanco and southern Camarón approaches beside Tlalixcoyan and distinguishes the lagoon complex from its outer marine mouth. Together these sources cover the fragment join, northward lower route and lagoon terminal at generalized scale; they do not support treating the modeled sea endpoint as the outer Gulf mouth.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected headward mountain feeder
correspondence.finding: The retained initial reach lies in a small west-to-east mountain valley. Original detailed topography shows that feeder entering the braided Marsh Fork valley from the west. It is not the southern mapped Marsh Fork headwater continuation. The feeder has no established name in the inspected original map.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary feeder and confluence scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Initial feeder name remains null; do not call every selected headwater reach Marsh Fork or Canning.

correspondence.component_scope: Marsh Fork mountain corridor
correspondence.finding: From the feeder confluence the selected course follows the labeled Marsh Fork Canning River eastward, then north through the long mountain valley. The valley bends slightly west and then northeast before its confluence with the eastern Canning trunk. Original FWS Map 5-3 separately shows Marsh Fork and the Canning mainstem and supports their junction; section 5.3 describes Marsh Fork as the major western tributary.
correspondence.correspondence: Continuous mountain corridor and material junction supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Marsh Fork Canning River is a distinct named tributary reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Marsh Fork–Canning confluence and upper Canning
correspondence.finding: The selected route joins the Canning from the west and turns generally north/northwest into the broader braided valley. The upstream Canning branch coming from the southeast is outside this selected route. The repeated Canning River label is placed on the downstream shared trunk, not merely near its basin.
correspondence.correspondence: Confluence and downstream continuation supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Canning River supports the provisional representative system candidate, without renaming its Marsh Fork tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Central mountain-front and foothill trunk
correspondence.finding: Overlapping original views follow the Canning past the Cache Creek valley and the Nanook/Ignek tributary-valley setting, around its westward mountain-front bend and into the coastal plain. The eastern tributaries remain separate from the selected north-running trunk; Kavik River is a separate western drainage. No substantial lake passage is present on this established corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported continuously at ordinary valley and junction scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Repeated Canning River trunk labels; tributaries retain their own separate scope.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Canning and delta division
correspondence.finding: The lower selected reach follows the Canning north through the coastal plain to a broad braided distributary area. Original topography distinguishes eastern Canning channels and the western Staines River route. FWS Map 5-2 and the section 5.2 overview independently show/describes the broad multiple-distributary delta.
correspondence.correspondence: Lower trunk, branching setting and approach to the western Staines-side channel belt supported.
correspondence.name_scope: A Canning-system delta setting is supported; it does not imply one name for each distributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected western coastal wetland and pond continuation
correspondence.finding: The selected northern continuation leaves the continuously mapped Staines route toward a farther-west wetland/pond belt. The detailed original view shows small southern channel ends, ponds, a larger unnamed northern lake, and lake/outlet channels. It does not show the watercourse link across the intervening wetland needed to join those networks along the selected continuation. The labeled Staines River remains to the east and drains by its own mapped outlet.
correspondence.correspondence: Material connection unresolved. Nearby channels and system membership are insufficient to claim the missing link.
correspondence.name_scope: No name established for the unresolved western connector or the selected terminal creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal and receiving water
correspondence.finding: The selected endpoint lies in the coastal lagoon landward of the barrier-island coast, west of Brownlow Point. Original cartography distinguishes this position from the mapped main Staines mouth farther east. NOAA Coast Pilot 9 chapter 9, paragraph 262, identifies the western Canning discharge setting as the lagoon southwest of Brownlow Point and describes its delta shoals. This corroborates the receiving-water setting only; it does not establish the missing western freshwater connector.
correspondence.correspondence: Receiving lagoon setting inspected; exact incoming-channel identity and continuous source correspondence remain unresolved.
correspondence.name_scope: Do not replace the selected endpoint with the better-labeled Staines or Canning mouths, and do not assert a uniform river name across lagoon water.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual initial Ashmere Lake passage and Bennett Brook feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected start is within the Ashmere Lake setting in Hinsdale, including the southern lake passage near and south of the Route143 neck. The southern outlet leads down Bennett Brook, which turns west across the low wetland corridor after the Tracy Brook junction and meets the northbound East Branch Housatonic River. The main East Branch continues separately southward upstream of that junction; that southern headward route is not the selected beginning.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: Ashmere Lake and Bennett Brook are directly labelled on the original map. Neither is assigned the scalar name Housatonic River. Plunkett Reservoir and its Frisell Brook outlet are separate western tributary features, not the selected initial lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Northbound East Branch through Hinsdale and the Dalton/Center Pond setting
correspondence.finding: Below Bennett Brook the selected corridor follows the East Branch north through Hinsdale, turns northwest toward Dalton, passes the Cleveland Brook connection, and runs through the Center Pond/outlet setting before turning west. The map shows the separate Wahconah Falls Brook approach at Center Pond. Cleveland Brook Reservoir and Windsor Reservoir are upstream tributary waterbodies rather than selected main-route lake passages.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: East Branch Housatonic River and Center Pond are direct map labels; the East Branch identity remains distinct from the lower Housatonic mainstem.

correspondence.component_scope: Dalton–Pittsfield East Branch and mainstem junction
correspondence.finding: The original map traces the East Branch west through Dalton and Coltsville, south at Adams Junction, then southwest through Pittsfield to the junction with the river approaching from the west. Unkamet Brook and Brattle Brook enter separately along this corridor. West Branch Housatonic River and the westward upstream mainstem approach are distinct mapped waterways; the selection follows the East Branch approach and then the southbound Housatonic.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: The original labels East Branch Housatonic River above the confluence and Housatonic River below it. The MassDEP prose independently locates the East Branch/mainstem meeting at Fred Garner Park, Pittsfield.

correspondence.component_scope: Pittsfield–Lenox–Lee corridor and Woods Pond
correspondence.finding: The selected river continues south through the meandering floodplain past New Lenox, into Woods Pond near Lenox Station, out through Lenox Dale, and downstream through Lee. The lake entry, outlet, and continuing channel are visible. Separate lateral brooks and nearby reservoirs are not used as substitutes for the selected route.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: Housatonic River and Woods Pond are directly labelled. The reservoir/pond passage retains its own identity.
correspondence.map_coverage: Overlapping headward and Massachusetts original maps; Massachusetts northern detail

correspondence.component_scope: South Lee–Stockbridge–Great Barrington–Sheffield and the state-line corridor
correspondence.finding: The map shows the river turning west from South Lee through Stockbridge and Glendale, then south past Housatonic/Risingdale and Van Deusenville to Great Barrington, Sheffield and Ashley Falls. Channel widenings/impoundments and their connecting reaches remain visible; the inspected view does not establish a separate name for every small widening. The Williams River, Green River and Hubbard Brook approaches are distinguishable from the selected main river. The selection continues along the Housatonic into Connecticut rather than switching to an eastern tributary.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: Repeated Housatonic River labels support the corridor. Local pond or tributary labels are not propagated over the whole selection.
correspondence.map_coverage: Massachusetts original, middle and southern details; overlap with Connecticut-upper original

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Connecticut, Falls Village, Cornwall and Kent
correspondence.finding: The channel remains continuous from the state-line/Canaan setting through the Blackberry River and Hollenbeck River junction settings, the Great Falls/Falls Village impounded reach and the subsequent southbound river. It continues past Lime Rock, West Cornwall, Cornwall Bridge and North Kent to Kent. The Salmon Creek approach and other lateral streams are separate. All intervening bends and valley transitions are mapped at corridor scale.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: Housatonic River is repeatedly labelled through this reach. Great Falls and Falls Village are supporting mapped landmarks; the Connecticut agency prose corroborates the same downstream sequence.

correspondence.component_scope: Bulls Bridge, Tenmile junction and Gaylordsville–New Milford
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor follows the Housatonic past the Bulls Bridge impounded setting and the separate Tenmile River entry from the west, then turns southeast through Gaylordsville toward New Milford. The Rocky River/Lake Candlewood connection and Aspetuck tributary approaches occur laterally. The route continues down the Housatonic through New Milford and toward Lovers Leap; it does not traverse Lake Candlewood.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: Housatonic River, Tenmile River, Rocky River and Lake Candlewood are direct map labels with different scopes. The model route is not named after any of these tributary or adjacent-lake features.
correspondence.map_coverage: Connecticut-upper southern detail and Connecticut-lakes northern detail

correspondence.component_scope: Lovers Leap, Lake Lillinonah, Shepaug arm and lower outlet
correspondence.finding: The map shows the Still River connection near the northern lake entrance/Lovers Leap setting, the southward then eastward Lake Lillinonah passage past Brookfield and Bridgewater, and the separate northern Shepaug River arm. The selected route stays on the Housatonic/Lillinonah axis, continues around the broad southern bend, and narrows into the outlet reach leading to the upper Lake Zoar corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: Both Housatonic River and Lake Lillinonah appear on the original. The Shepaug River arm remains a distinct tributary arm; it is not traversed upward by the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper and lower Lake Zoar, including the FID boundary
correspondence.finding: After the Lillinonah outlet, the selection continues east/southeast along the connected Housatonic channel and the upper Lake Zoar reach, passing separate Pomperaug and Pootatuck tributary entries. The division between FID9774 and FID9775 is within this continuous lake/river corridor, not an independently named river break. FID9775 follows the long southeastward lake passage through Riverside and the narrows at Stevenson.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: Lake Zoar and Housatonic River are directly labelled on the original. A model fragment boundary is not treated as a naming boundary.
correspondence.map_coverage: Connecticut-lakes southern detail and overlapping lower-estuary northern detail

correspondence.component_scope: Stevenson–Derby lower impoundment and Naugatuck junction
correspondence.finding: Below the Stevenson narrows the selected channel follows the lower elongated impounded river to the Derby/Shelton setting and then the Naugatuck River confluence. The lower map labels Housatonic River along this waterway and shows its connection throughout. Connecticut DEEP identifies the third major riverine impoundment as Lake Housatonic and places the tidal reach below Derby Dam.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: Housatonic River and Naugatuck River are direct map labels. Lake Housatonic is the supporting primary-prose waterbody name, not claimed as a label observed in this map export.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower estuary and actual Milford-side coastal terminal setting
correspondence.finding: From the Naugatuck junction the selected route continues down the broad estuary through the Shelton/Orange and Stratford/Milford corridor, past islands and bars, then toward the Nells Island/Cedar Beach–Milford Point shoreline complex. The terminal-detail original shows the main Housatonic channel bending around the west and south of Nells Island, the tidal-marsh branches behind Milford Point, and the adjacent open coastal water. The selected generalized terminal is understood in this estuarine/outer-shore setting, not asserted to be the exact main-channel mouth or a precise coast vertex. The lower river and its receiving Long Island Sound setting are corroborated by primary agency prose.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no exact-bank or vertex agreement asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: Housatonic River, Nells Island, Cedar Beach, Milford Point, Sniffens Point and Stratford Point are mapped separately. No river scalar name is assigned to every tidal-marsh or shoreline connection.
correspondence.map_coverage: Lower-estuary original, middle/mouth details, plus terminal estuarine-shoreline original

correspondence.component_scope: western headward feeder east of Caetés
correspondence.finding: The Capoeiras original depicts the small east/northeast-running feeder in the Bastões setting and its connection into the Riacho do Mel corridor. This accounts for the selected western approach, including its northward bend, before the route turns southeast. The map also distinguishes the separate Riacho São Pedro or Fundo approach farther south. The small selected initial feeder is not assigned that southern stream's label.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary headward-corridor scale; initial hydronym unresolved

correspondence.component_scope: Riacho do Mel, Cajarana and upper Canhoto connection
correspondence.finding: The Capoeiras map labels Riacho do Mel on the southward approach and Rio Canhoto on the eastward continuation around the Cajarana/Roncaria setting. Its generalized depiction does not establish a modern reservoir shoreline. The original SGB longitudinal network diagram independently places Barragem Cajarana on the upper Canhoto before Canhotinho and shows continuous downstream connection. The diagram supplies the named impoundment's longitudinal connection; the maps supply the geographic corridor. The neighboring upper-Mundaú Cajueiro and Inhaúma/Inhumas impoundments are explicitly separate branches.
correspondence.correspondence: complete ordinary corridor and material reservoir connection; not a reservoir-bank survey

correspondence.component_scope: Canhotinho–São José da Laje Canhoto reach
correspondence.finding: The SGB original hydrographic maps show the named northern river passing east through the Canhotinho station/town setting, turning southeast toward São José da Laje and then south. This sequence corresponds to the selected route rather than the southwestern upper Mundaú. The Inhaúma enters from the west below the São José da Laje station; the separately mapped Mocambo/Inhaúma branch is not included as the selected headward course.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Canhoto–Mundaú junction and União dos Palmares
correspondence.finding: Both original SGB maps and the longitudinal diagram distinguish the Canhoto arriving from the north from the upper Mundaú arriving from Correntes and Santana do Mundaú to the west. They join upstream of the União dos Palmares station/town reach, after which the mapped southward river is Mundaú. This material junction is directly covered rather than inferred from a basin label or model connectivity.
correspondence.correspondence: complete junction and downstream name correspondence

correspondence.component_scope: União dos Palmares–Murici–Rio Largo lower river
correspondence.finding: The SGB basin maps follow the Mundaú south/southeast through the Murici-Ponte and Fazenda Boa Fortuna/Rio Largo settings to the lagoon approach. The Maceió original overlaps the lower river below Rio Largo, labels Rio Mundaú above Satuba and shows the river continuing through the lowland channel network into the northwestern part of Lagoa Mundaú. The western Rio Satuba and smaller local approaches remain separate tributary lines.
correspondence.correspondence: complete overlapping lower-river corridor

correspondence.component_scope: Lagoa Mundaú and actual southern Atlantic-outlet setting
correspondence.finding: The Maceió 1:100,000 original visibly carries the lower river into the lagoon northwest of Fernão Velho, shows the open lagoon east of Coqueiro Seco, and the southern island/channel system beside Trapiche da Barra and the Atlantic coastal barrier. The channels continue through the coastal outlet system toward the ocean. This establishes the selected lagoon passage and sea-terminal setting at ordinary corridor scale. The larger Lagoa Manguaba to the west and its separate incoming Rio Paraíba are clearly distinguished and are not substituted for the selected passage. No unique hydronym is imposed on every coastal channel, and no exact inlet-point or bank agreement is claimed.
correspondence.correspondence: complete lagoon, material outlet connection and ordinary coastal terminal setting
